cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1), and he's just called himself and the others with him God's fellow workers (2 Corinthians 6:1). Now he says they put no obstacle in anyone's way. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer BEING the obstacle, and anybody digging for the tape had to shove me aside first.

cards.question: Why does Paul make sure he and the others serving with him put no obstacle in anyone's way?

answers.text: So no one can discredit their ministry
So the leaders in Jerusalem approve
So their travels go more smoothly

cards.text: Instead, Paul says, they commend themselves in every way. Then he reads off his credentials: great endurance, troubles, hardships and calamities.

cards.question: Through great endurance in troubles, hardships and calamities, Paul and the others commend themselves as ___ of God.

cards.text: Then it gets rougher: beatings, imprisonments, riots, labor, sleepless nights and hunger. Most folks fill a résumé with their wins, and Paul's reads BEATEN, LOCKED UP, NO SLEEP.

cards.question: Paul lists beatings, prison and hunger as proof that God has walked away from him and the others.

cards.text: Then the list turns. It stops being about what happened to them and starts being about how they live while it's happening.

cards.question: Paul's list turns from what he and the others go through to how they live as servants of God. Which pair shows up on it now?

cards.text: Along with purity and kindness, the list holds knowledge, patience, the Holy Spirit, sincere love, truthful speech and the power of God. Friend, this résumé needs a SECOND PAGE.

cards.question: Then Paul pulls a picture from the battlefield. He says he and the others carry the weapons of righteousness. In which hand?

answers.text: In the right hand and in the left

cards.text: Now Paul starts pairing up things that pull in opposite directions. He and the others serve God through glory and dishonor.

cards.question: In Paul's pairs, glory goes with dishonor. In the next pair, what goes with slander?
Paul says people view him and the others as imposters, yet they are ___.

cards.text: They're unknown yet well-known, dying and yet living on. Friend, I got left for dead in the back of a junk drawer, and LOOK at me now: mustache fuller than EVER.

cards.question: Paul keeps the pairs coming. He says he and the others are punished, yet not ___.

cards.text: They're sorrowful, yet always rejoicing. That's you at the airport sending your best friend off to a dream job: crying, cheering, and security is VERY confused.

cards.question: Paul says he and the others are poor. But what are they doing at the same time?
Paul says that because he and the others have nothing, they possess nothing either.

cards.text: Then Paul puts the list down and speaks straight to them: "We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide."

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians that the affection being held back is his own, not theirs.

cards.text: Paul asks for a fair exchange, and he says he's speaking to them as to his children. Friend, I KNOW that voice, because six little cutters on one counter heard it from me plenty.

cards.question: Paul's heart is open wide toward the Corinthians. What does he ask them to do in return?

findings.problem: The wrong answer "famous" is true elsewhere in the passage. In 2 Corinthians 6:9, Paul says he and the others are "well-known," so a baker could argue that "famous" fits.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.
